decisions.mark: states that MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY is the gate, and that it is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Set `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` in your `mbedtls_config.h`. | WHY: The answer says MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY must be set to enable the facility, but it never says the option is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h.

decisions.mark: concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
decisions.detail: QUOTE: **Default build:** `platform.h:166-167` maps `mbedtls_calloc` to `calloc` and `mbedtls_free` to `free`, so there is no indirection. | WHY: The answer states that in a default build the macros map directly to calloc/free with no indirection.

decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Set `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... The macros win over any runtime setting... Set only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, leave the macros undefined, and call once during startup... `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is only declared in the runtime configuration. Calling it when the macros are set is a compile error. | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter. It also says the setter is not declared when the macros are set, so calling it is a compile error, which makes the two mutually exclusive.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is only declared in the runtime configuration. Calling it when the macros are set is a compile error. | WHY: The answer says the function is only declared in the runtime configuration, so with the macros set it is not declared and calling it fails to compile. Together with "`platform.c`'s pointer block is compiled out", this covers the "neither declared nor compiled" claim.

decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`calloc` returns NULL and `free` does nothing until you call the setter." | WHY: The answer states that the default stubs (when no STD_CALLOC/FREE is defined) return NULL for calloc and do nothing for free, so they fail rather than fall back.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`) ... installs its own `buffer_alloc_calloc` and `buffer_alloc_free` through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()`. | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator uses the runtime setter from its init function, but it never says it is the only in-tree user of that setter.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: If `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, it installs the mutexed variants and initializes `heap.mutex`. | WHY: The answer says that `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init` installs mutexed variants when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is on, and that it otherwise installs its plain `buffer_alloc_calloc`/`buffer_alloc_free`. It places this in the init function. The compile-time nature is implied by the macro condition.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "It needs `MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C` plus the platform layer." | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator needs the platform layer, but it never says it requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY or that enabling the buffer allocator alone won't route the library's allocations through it.
